newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars to support won - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars to support won - dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea intervened in late morning trading on Thursday, selling dollars at 859.20/50 won per dollar to support the won, dealers said.
"The Bank of Korea intervened to boost the won," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said the won rose to 858.90 soon after the central bank's intervention. But it fell again to 859.20 just before the morning close.
The won opened trading at 859.00 and moved from 858.60 to 859.40.
Dealers said the won briefly rose in early morning trading on fears of the Bank of Korea's dollar buying.
Unwinding of dollar positions helped limit the won's steep fall in morning trading, they said.
